channel.title: Eshan Roy — Engineering Journal & Research Publications
channel.description: Systems engineering, autonomous AI coding runtimes, Linux engineering, and open-source infrastructure.

item.title: [Journal] Engineering OpenMail: Modern Self-Hosted Mail Infrastructure with Zero-CLI Configuration
item.description: Why self-hosted email infrastructure remains essential for digital sovereignty, and how OpenMail bridges legacy IMAP/SMTP protocols with modern reactive web ergonomics.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Journal] High-Performance Concurrency in Rust: Lessons from Building Veda and Polaris
item.description: Practical lessons learned building low-latency parallel runtimes, lock-free work-stealing deques, and declarative procedural macro engines in production Rust.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Research] Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Benchmarks for Sub-8B Small Language Models
item.description: Deploying generative intelligence on edge hardware and single-GPU developer workstations requires rigorous parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) of Small Language Models (SLMs) in the 1B to 8B parameter range. This report documents the empirical evaluation underlying SLMGen. We analyze LoRA rank sensitivity, 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization degradation, and dataset token hygiene heuristics across Phi-3.5, Llama-3.2, and Qwen-2.5 base models.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Journal] Why Chatbots Fail at Coding: Enforcing Deterministic Policy Gates in Autonomous Agents
item.description: Why prompt engineering alone cannot secure AI coding agents, and how compiled AST verification and non-bypassable policy gates turn unpredictable model outputs into reliable repository mutations.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Research] Adaptive Work-Stealing Scheduling & NUMA Affinity in Rust Task Runtimes
item.description: Parallel task scheduling across modern multi-socket hardware encounters severe throughput degradation from cross-NUMA interconnect contention and false cache-line sharing. We present the design of Veda, a high-performance Rust parallel execution runtime implementing an adaptive work-stealing algorithm with NUMA node affinity pinning. Empirical benchmarks on 32-core and 64-core topologies demonstrate up to a 2.4x reduction in task dispatch latency compared to naive work-stealing.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Journal] Designing Kyro: Local-First Desktop Automation with Tauri v2, Rust, and MCP
item.description: How we built Kyro, a local-first autonomous desktop AI agent that bridges screen understanding and real computer use with zero-trust local SQLite privacy and OS Keyring security.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Research] Empirical Verification in Terminal AI Runtimes: Non-Bypassable Policy Gates and Isolated Sandboxing
item.description: This technical report presents the design and empirical evaluation of the verification engine within M31A. We investigate the failure modes of ambient shell execution in language model agents, analyze process isolation mechanisms across Linux cgroups v2 and macOS Seatbelt, and benchmark a two-phase SQLite WAL crash-recovery architecture capable of restoring consistent workspace states following abnormal process termination.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Journal] Architecting Snigdha OS: Custom Kernel Switching, Minimal Arch Base, and i3wm Workstation Ergonomics
item.description: How we engineered an Arch-based Linux ecosystem tailored for developer productivity, systems programming, and penetration testing, featuring custom kernel tooling and automated PKGBUILD pipelines.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Journal] Inside M31A: Building a Rust-Native Autonomous Engineering Runtime
item.description: A comprehensive architectural breakdown of M31A, explaining why intelligence is not authority, how the 10-tier downward module hierarchy functions, and how two-phase SQLite recovery prevents workspace corruption.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)

item.title: [Research] Towards Autonomous Development Systems: A Research Framework
item.description: We propose a research framework for autonomous software development systems — computational runtimes capable of reasoning over, modifying, and verifying complex software repositories under strict safety guarantees. We define the problem space separating conversational assistants from sovereign execution runtimes, formalize an 11-stage non-bypassable policy gating model, and introduce empirical verification criteria where language model assertions are treated as untrusted until mathematically and observationally proven.
item.author: m.eshanized@gmail.com (Eshan Roy)
